column1: 1|core_match|P3|Beer is a bulk interspecies commodity.|Industrial casks suit the commodity and reused reference packaging.|Keep robust bulk packaging; brewery labels may improve differentiation.

2|partial|P2|Prestige wines travel by the case in containers adapted to loss of gravity.|Loose bottles identify wine, but the distinctive shipping protection is absent.|Add an optional restrained transport case or cradle without replacing the reference bottles.

3|core_match|P3|Panther Sweat is a notorious very strong luxury beverage, not literal animal sweat.|The animal-shaped novelty decanter follows the icon and does not imply biological sweat.|Refine premium beverage presentation; do not literalise the name.

4|partial|P2|Designer non-alcoholic cream-and-honey liqueur contains herbal extracts.|The bottles are recognisable, but clear glass without distinct creamy contents weakens the product identity.|Represent opaque cream/honey contents and designer labelling rather than ordinary clear wine.
5|core_match|P3|Vintage champagne is an expensive bulk-traded luxury.|Foil-neck champagne bottles are consistent with that identity.|Keep premium closure/labels; a shipping case is optional context.

6|partial|P1|Premium Lumiere is a bright green glowing brew shown in crystal urns; cheap grades use opaque jars.|Crystal-like urns are appropriate, but emission is attached to the vessel material rather than a distinct brew.|Separate glowing liquid from crystal shell and show a convincing fill level.

7|ambiguous|P1|Bristol makes mouth-blown coloured wine glasses, brandy balloons and champagne flutes only.|The model follows the icon's carafe-like centrepiece, which conflicts with the text's restriction.|Retain the evidence conflict explicitly; establish its intended drinking-vessel form before replacing it.

8|core_match|P2|Cantata makes individually commissioned cut glass in runs of at most two dozen of one design.|Related cut-crystal vessels fit the bespoke range and small group size.|Improve distinct cutting patterns and hand-finished variation; do not turn it into mass-produced identical stock.
9|core_match|P2|Velvet is a luxury fabric with deep pile.|The roll/sheet and matte tinted sheen identify velvet.|Refine visible pile and soft edge thickness at close range.

10|core_match|P2|Silk is a luxury fabric popular with several cultures.|A draped silk roll is suitable; directional sheen differentiates it from velvet.|Keep a fine weave and restrained lustre rather than lacquer-like highlights.

11|partial|P2|Watered silk owes its rarity to a complex weave.|The roll is suitable but the distinctive watered/moire appearance is weak after generic fabric shading.|Restore a deliberate moire weave rather than only random noise.

12|core_match|P2|Raw silk has a particular texture appreciated by Achaeans and Mikotaj.|The rougher matte roll is consistent; the lore's sound preference is not visible in a still.|Strengthen irregular slubs and coarse fibres without claiming an implemented acoustic effect.

13|core_match|P2|Satin taffeta is a rare, expensive social fabric.|The sheet/roll and directional highlights are appropriate.|Refine fine weave and crisp folds while retaining its difference from silk.

14|core_match|P2|Old Terran Egyptian sea-cotton is exceptionally fine and expensive.|The pale cotton roll is compatible with the product.|Use convincing fine fibres and soft edges; provenance cannot be proved by shape alone.

15|partial|P2|Achaean angora is combed fur from pet felines.|The yarn spool is plausible, but looks more like a smooth wound thread than soft feline angora.|Add a restrained fuzzy fibre halo and irregular yarn strands.

16|core_match|P2|The tiara/bracelet set is raw opal with metachrome.|The separate tiara and bracelet now use unfaceted raw opals and metachrome settings/chain; introduced diamond identities are removed.|Further refine opal colour play and jewellery workmanship without changing the two-piece composition.

17|partial|P1|A woven red-gold band carries an eight-point gold sunburst, central aquamarine and scattered brilliants.|The band, sunburst and centre exist; woven construction and surrounding brilliants are missing.|Model the woven ribbon and scattered small stones; preserve the eight-point motif.

18|core_match|P3|A square-cut emerald must be set in white gold.|The revised emerald has a square seven-ring step cut with small chamfered corners, white-gold bezel and corner claws.|Retain the square cut and white-gold identity during future detail work.

19|core_match|P3|The brooch uses a cabochon-cut ruby with red gold and copper.|The revised ruby is a smooth domed cabochon, with actual sheet thickness and visibly differentiated red-gold/copper petals.|Further engraving is optional; retain the unfaceted cabochon and two metals.

20|core_match|P3|Exactly 23 astramarines are set in white gold and titanium.|Actual Blender inspection counts 23 astramarines and white-gold bezels, with 22 titanium links; the studio render is visibly a pale setting.|Retain the exact stone count and white-gold/titanium distinction.

21|core_match|P2|The eternity ring combines ultropaz and alexandrite in 24ct yellow gold.|The yellow-gold ring now carries four amber ultropaz and four violet-studio-state alexandrite gems; pearl/astramarine identities are removed.|Refine the tiny settings; dynamic alexandrite colour change remains unimplemented and is not certified by this still.

22|partial|P2|The pectoral combines diamond, emerald and metachrome.|The gem/lattice composition is recognisable, but the framework is labelled white gold/platinum rather than metachrome.|Give the framework a deliberate metachrome identity; refine lattice workmanship.

23|partial|P2|Seventeen blue opals are paired with a white-gold clasp.|Stone count and pale clasp are present; the stones share an astramarine-style transparent shader.|Give blue opals their own material character and refine their settings.
24|core_match|P2|The bracelet has three pearl strands and platinum.|The model has three strands, pearls and a pale metallic clasp.|Refine nacre lustre and the clasp; do not add arbitrary gemstones.

25|core_match|P3|The item is diamond; its reputation is a cultural/marketing point.|Faceted clear warm stones are appropriate.|Keep diamond-like refraction; rarity is not a visual acceptance criterion.

26|core_match|P2|Emeralds are rare and flawless specimens are exceptionally unusual.|Green faceted stones identify emerald; the current stones are unusually clean.|Subtle inclusions would suit common trade specimens, but flawless examples are not forbidden by lore.
27|core_match|P3|Sapphires may be blue, yellow or white.|Blue faceted stones are a valid selection.|Additional colour variants are optional, not required corrections.
28|core_match|P3|Rubies are rarer than diamonds.|Red faceted stones are compatible.|Retain ruby colour/absorption; economic rarity cannot be inferred from a still.

29|core_match|P3|Ultropaz comes from a few remote planets.|Amber stones follow the icon; the text does not specify optical properties.|Treat the optical response as an interpretation, not a measured canonical material.

30|partial|P2|Alexandrite changes colour between natural and artificial illumination.|A fixed purple shader depicts one condition but not the defining change.|Provide a paired-light study or a controlled colour-change material; avoid claiming current behaviour is implemented.

31|core_match|P2|Metachrome can be cut as a gem and melted into settings.|The cut-stone state is a valid representation of one use.|Keep its dual gem/setting identity consistent across jewellery; exact optics remain speculative.

32|partial|P2|Opal is a culturally prized Old Terran gem.|Generic clear faceted green glass with inclusions is weakly distinct as opal.|Develop opal-like body colour/colour play as a visual interpretation, guided by the icon.

33|core_match|P2|Pearls retain their lustre and are especially prized by Artemia.|Smooth lustrous pearls are appropriate.|Refine nacre and small natural irregularities without making them faceted stones.

34|partial|P2|Moonstone is a revived semi-precious gem popular across cultures.|A generic faceted green shader is not very distinctive as moonstone.|Explore restrained moonstone-like internal sheen; that material detail is an analogue, not specified game physics.

35|core_match|P3|Astramarine is a sophisticated Mikotaj gift.|Cyan gems follow the reference and suit a precious gift commodity.|Exact optical behaviour is unspecified; keep its identity distinct from blue opal in other items.

36|core_match|P3|Peridot is especially valued by Braccatia as the colour of honour.|Yellow-green stones preserve the relevant colour association.|Keep this colour identity; do not invent heraldic text as recovered canon.

37|core_match|P3|Amethyst remains popular despite a false historical sobriety belief.|Purple stones represent the gem correctly.|Do not turn the historical belief into a functioning protective effect.

38|core_match|P2|Artemian abstract sculpture is meaningful metalwork, prized by collectors.|Curved metal forms on a plinth fit the description.|Refine intentional form/line and craft; emotional meaning is not independently verifiable.

39|partial|P1|Artemian furniture blends sculpture with exotic-metal curves and planes.|The curved table fits; the generic shelf and storage block poorly express that sculptural culture.|Remodel the set as coherent sculptural metal furniture, preserving the reference composition.

40|partial|P2|Braccatian export horns are oversized decorative work with Saxon/Celtic affinities.|Horns and metal bands fit; distinctive workmanship and relative scale are underdeveloped.|Develop carved/knot-like bands from reference evidence; keep ceremonial originals distinct from export decoration.

41|core_match|P2|Braccatian leatherwork is exceptional, custom-made and the finest pieces are rarely legally traded.|The remodelled tailored coat, boots and belt now show thickness, folds and raised decoration.|Continue fine leather craft and culturally compatible ornament; do not label invented details as recovered.

42|partial|P1|Braccatian exports are elegant, archaic ornamental weapons.|Sword/flail fit; the third flat triangle with bars loses the handled ornate blade seen in the icon and is described inconsistently as an instrument.|Resolve the triangular weapon/guard geometry and grip; do not reinterpret it as a harp from the bars alone.

43|partial|P2|Four quail-egg-sized dark chocolates contain glowing Lumiere and come in an exquisite box.|Four chocolate orbs and a decorative box are present; confectionery craftsmanship is very basic.|Refine the box/interior and edible chocolate finish; a cutaway could clarify filling but closed orbs need not expose it.

44|core_match|P2|Eggs of metre-tall Rigellian ants are a costly delicacy.|Large smooth egg shapes are consistent.|Improve shell texture; racial scale is not verifiable from display-normalised objects alone.

45|core_match|P2|The snack consists of pearls dissolved in brandy.|The flask now has an actual hollow glass wall and amber brandy volume with subtle nacre scattering; there are no whole pearl bead objects. The current render was inspected.|Further develop the delicate dissolved-nacre appearance and authored bottle label; do not reintroduce intact pearls.

46|partial|P2|Goats' ear mushrooms are a rare, limited-harvest delicacy.|Mushrooms are recognisable, but current caps/stems remain generic.|Use the original cap shapes and organic detail to establish species character without assuming the name dictates exact anatomy.

47|core_match|P3|Sweetcorn is scarce premium organic produce, favoured by vegetarian Artemia.|Individual kernels/cobs in a produce crate match the commodity.|Keep fresh organic character rather than depicting the blight as the sale product.

48|core_match|P2|Kulos cheese is rare, dense and nourishing dairy from a low-yield animal.|A waxed cut cheese wheel is consistent; hole/wax details follow the icon, not explicit lore.|Retain repaired cut-face topology; develop realistic rind/wax/curd texture in later refinement.

49|core_match|P2|Grains are basic bulk staples across species.|Bulk sacks are a sensible representation.|Improve folds, ties and cloth construction; no specific grain anatomy is mandated for sealed sacks.

50|partial|P2|Marine kelp, phosphoran and mossweed are inexpensive staples.|Lattice crates fit bulk cargo, but generic green ovals read more as leaves than marine fronds.|Refine ribbon/frond/branching forms while preserving the cargo arrangement.
51|core_match|P3|Krill is a cheap freeze-dried survival staple.|Plain bulk canisters fit dry processed food.|Keep utilitarian packaging; do not make it a fresh seafood luxury display.

52|core_match|P3|Clean water is precious, heavily shipped and legally protected.|A rack of sealed bulk tanks fits this role.|Cargo/water identification may help; the contents need not be visible through metal tanks.

53|partial|P2|Ortok's Mansions has ten truth and ten deceit mansions, Tarot-like player pieces and a highest truth goal.|The corrected set has ten truth and ten deceit locations across six tiers, the highest truth goal and four illustrative arcana-like character tokens. Its boards, staircase and craftsmanship remain simpler than the icon.|Add the sculpted staircase and richer Rigellian workmanship while preserving the verified 20-location split; the token motifs/colour coding remain authored interpretations.

54|partial|P2|Brutos's unique fear-sensitive goggles are historical Maunid military memorabilia.|The goggles are recognisable but generic; fear sensing itself is not visible in a still.|Refine a distinctive historical instrument and wear; do not invent the unknown mechanism as canon.

55|core_match|P2|Huskar cigars are brown-paper rolls in brilliant wooden boxes; smoke is purple if lit.|The coloured wooden box and brown cigars fit an unlit product display.|Refine wrappers/brand craftsmanship; any later lit view must use purple smoke.

56|partial|P2|Maunik's Cube is a heavy, oily metal puzzle with uncoloured faces bearing Law-of-the-Cube slogans.|The 3x3 metal cube fits, but repeated crosses do not convey inscriptions and the finish is rather dry.|Add oily metal response and authored inscription-like strokes without claiming readable canonical language.

57|core_match|P2|The unique gong marks a foundational Braccatian uprising.|A suspended historical gong fits the object.|Develop singular craftsmanship and age; avoid inventing a recovered revolutionary emblem.

58|partial|P1|HoloStar Globes are holographic charts of limited explored space, kept as family heirlooms.|The glass globe/stand is plausible, but latitude bands suggest a globe more than a holographic star chart.|Add a legible internal star/route-sector composition rather than a generic planet globe.

59|core_match|P2|Besthelda's Apothecary is a rare boxed collection of expertly compounded natural remedies.|A fitted case with many glass vials fits the collection.|Refine differentiated contents, stoppers and historical hand-labelled craft.

60|partial|P1|Photoplasmic cocoons contain modulated frozen light for therapy.|The glowing egg/suspended spheres hint at light, but read mainly as a glass ornament.|Develop structured luminous photoplasm and a coherent therapeutic enclosure; exact mechanism/scale is unspecified.

61|partial|P1|Steam Racers are heavy Braccatian steam-era arena machines with rear explosive-harpoon tailgunners.|Boiler, stacks, wheels and a rear gun are present, but the model is toy-like and lacks a convincing tailgunner emplacement.|Refine a heavy classic steam racer with readable rear gunner station, not a generic toy locomotive.

62|partial|P1|KKZ Quad uses one 100-card deck for two duellists and two magistrates; execution cards define the dangerous game.|Generic green decks and pip-like faces read as ordinary playing cards.|Establish the deck/four-role identity and authored execution-card language visually, with restrained sealed technical details.

63|ambiguous|P1|Kraagil Oil comes from an endangered whale/dragon-like aquatic crustacean.|The original icon depicts the animal; the model preserves this metonymy but reduces it to a spiked segmented form.|Refine the specific head/body/frond anatomy; do not replace the canonical animal icon automatically with a generic oil bottle.

64|core_match|P2|The axe is a revered, rare Artemian ritual object associated with Moon Goddess Cyreni.|The rebuilt solid crescent head and turned haft follow the reference; the new craft pass uses recessed lunar metalwork and carved wood.|Keep it a carefully made sacred artefact; lunar motifs are an authored interpretation, and rumoured sacrifice does not establish blood decoration.

65|partial|P2|The Horn of Plenty is an actual Braccatian ritual horn, unlike decorative export examples.|The single larger ornamented horn and chain distinguish it somewhat from the export set.|Refine unique ceremonial workmanship, historic use and ornament rather than only scaling the common horn.

66|partial|P1|Dionne's Lightwork is a singular famous artwork by Flic Spens.|The composition follows the icon, but a primitive figure and planes poorly express a finished masterpiece.|Refine the intentional sculptural form, pedestal and light medium; do not substitute an unrelated realistic portrait.

67|core_match|P2|The loving cup is an Achaean communal ritual centrepiece with individual history.|The corrected hollow cup is appropriate; handle clearance is now verified.|Refine individual handwork/history; red lining versus contents remains an icon interpretation, not settled lore.

68|partial|P2|Law of the Cube is a rare Maunid holy book in an obsolete script.|The cubic reliquary follows the icon, but a few strokes barely communicate a sacred text.|Develop inscription/reliquary detail; do not assume an alien book must be a Terran paper codex or invent a translation.

69|core_match|P3|Biofort is a spacer medicine and the specific counter to Silicon Death.|A medical case and vials fit the referenced product.|Use unambiguous product identification; therapeutic effect is not validated by a prop model.

70|core_match|P3|Vir-Attack is a broad in-universe medicine with specific exclusions and APV counters.|Medical packaging and vials are suitable.|Avoid claiming it cures every named condition; appearance alone cannot prove efficacy.

71|core_match|P2|Supa-Shellac treats Artemian chitin rot and is unusable by Terrans.|The labelled medicine bottle is appropriate.|Keep its Artemian medical identity; do not present it as a Terran cosmetic despite the name.

72|core_match|P2|Swat is the counter to the Artemia-targeting Shell Shock APV.|The sprayer can depict a medical preparation.|Keep treatment identity clear rather than implying it is a weapon against Artemia.

73|core_match|P3|Star Balm is a Mikotaj-produced antidote to Astrophobia.|The labelled balm bottle is compatible.|Use Mikotaj product identity and keep the Astrophobia association clear in the catalogue.

74|core_match|P3|Shell Shock is an agent-delivered fictional APV targeting Artemia; Swat is its counter.|A portable sealed case fits the delivery role.|Keep it distinct from the missile inventory; biological gameplay function is not visually validated.
75|core_match|P3|Phantom is an agent-delivered fictional APV affecting Mikotaj.|A carried sealed container is compatible.|Use product identity rather than inventing an unsupported visible mechanism.

76|core_match|P3|Judgement Day is a delayed agent-delivered fictional APV for several species.|A guarded portable payload canister is plausible.|Do not turn it into a conventional launchable missile merely because of the shape.

77|core_match|P3|Silicon Death is an agent-delivered fictional APV with a particular species pattern.|The carried sealed barrel is compatible with the icon.|Keep product and counterpart Biofort distinct; do not literalise the name as an asteroid-dissolving missile.

78|core_match|P3|Selenium is low-grade construction and missile ore.|Generic reused casks match the actual reference reuse.|Cargo labels can distinguish content; beer-cask reuse alone is not a lore error.
79|core_match|P3|Asteros is low-grade ore used to run the Powerplant.|The same bulk-cask family is icon-compatible.|Retain resource identity in metadata/labels; no unique ore appearance is specified.
80|core_match|P3|Barium is low-grade construction/missile/satellite ore.|Bulk casks suit the reference and commodity.|Do not infer real-world barium chemistry from the shared name.
81|core_match|P3|Crystalite is low-grade small-craft/Destructor/Vortex ore.|The reused cask packaging is canonical to the icon.|The name does not require visible crystals when the cargo is sealed.

82|core_match|P2|Quazinc is medium-grade ore for Napalm and Hellfire missiles.|The canister and separate yellow sample suit the reference.|Improve mineral morphology; exact optical/physical properties are unspecified.

83|core_match|P2|Bytanium is medium-grade SpaceDock/Nuclear ore.|The canister and brown sample fit the icon.|Keep sample colour/reference identity without inventing nuclear behaviour for the ore prop.
84|core_match|P2|Korellium is medium-grade cruiser/Stasis ore.|The canister and grey sample are compatible.|Do not add ice simply because one consumer is a Stasis missile.
85|core_match|P2|Dragonium is medium-grade construction ore.|Reinforced cases and a purple-grey sample follow the icon.|Refine the mineral surface; no dragon anatomy is implied by the name.

86|core_match|P2|Traxium is high-grade ore used for Virus missiles.|Valve-vessel packaging and a separate mineral sample follow the reference.|Physical storage state is unspecified; avoid claiming the flask proves it is a gas.
87|core_match|P2|Nexos is high-grade ore used for Mega missiles.|Red high-grade packaging and sample fit the icon.|Keep its economic identity separate from an assertion that it is itself a warhead.
88|core_match|P3|Explosive is the cheap general-purpose conventional missile.|A relatively simple closed warhead is compatible.|Do not overdecorate it as a uniquely precious ceremonial item.

89|core_match|P3|Area Explosive is a related missile with a wider destructive area.|The related, differentiated warhead family is suitable.|Blast radius is a gameplay property, not proved by model size.

90|core_match|P2|Napalm is an advanced plasma-gas incendiary device in this setting.|The specialised heat/payload assembly is compatible.|Avoid assuming a literal historical Terran fuel recipe or bottle form.

91|core_match|P3|Hellfire carries a destructive substance that spreads over an asteroid.|A specialised sealed missile is plausible.|Spreading behaviour requires a separate gameplay/VFX check, not a different still by default.

92|partial|P2|Scatter deploys several conventional explosive missiles over the target.|The carrier-like form hints at a special payload, but the sub-missile role is not clearly demonstrated.|Provide a readable payload-bay/separation study without claiming current deployment animation exists.
93|core_match|P2|Vortex releases a wandering electrical storm.|The specialised missile form is compatible.|Keep later VFX electrical; the name does not imply a black hole or gravitational vortex.
94|core_match|P3|Nuclear destroys structures and orbiting ships.|The marked nuclear missile is consistent.|Yield cannot be judged from display-normalised prop dimensions.

95|core_match|P2|Virus dissolves asteroid material rather than describing the personnel APVs.|The chemical/payload-like missile is compatible.|Keep it distinct from human/species infection imagery and the APV medicine family.
96|core_match|P2|Anti-Virus neutralises an asteroid virus and then itself.|A related neutralising missile is suitable.|Do not confuse it with crew pharmaceuticals or a universal biological cure.
97|core_match|P3|Mega destroys an entire asteroid.|A substantial specialised warhead is compatible.|Magnitude is a gameplay property; a still does not validate destructive capacity.
98|core_match|P2|Stasis suspends an asteroid through temporal physics.|The field-like missile presentation is compatible.|Do not render it as a literal ice or refrigeration weapon.

99|core_match|P3|Bug Hunter is an Artemia-specific fictional APV delivered by missile.|The missile rather than portable-case form is correct.|Keep its target/function identity in the catalogue; the prop does not validate a biological effect.

100|core_match|P3|Meat-Eater is a fictional APV missile for Achaean, Braccatian and Terran populations.|The dedicated missile form fits the delivery role.|Do not literalise the name with teeth or confuse it with the asteroid Virus payload.

101|core_match|P2|Information is illicit data about a subject supplied through the %s placeholder.|A folio is a valid reference-derived symbol for information; its strokes do not invent a fixed subject.|Keep the subject dynamic and avoid claiming the authored strokes are recovered text.
